dedupe_keys.name: digital twin for maintaining the lower mississippi and mcclellan kerr arkansas inland waterways

description: This case covers a University of Arkansas project (August 2021 to September 2023) that built a simulation-based digital twin of an inland waterway system to evaluate lock and dam disruptions and to plan maintenance. The team developed a Python-enhanced NetLogo agent-based simulation of vessel traffic through the lower Mississippi River system and the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System, with a spatiotemporal model of water levels fitted to over 315,000 hourly gauge readings at 18 sites and probabilistic models of lock failures from USACE lock closure data, and used deep reinforcement learning to choose repair and preventive maintenance actions that maximise cargo throughput. The final report, by Haitao Liao, Shengfan Zhang and colleagues under a US DOT University Transportation Centers grant, is on Zenodo together with a cleaned table of lock stoppages from 2000 to 2020 and a MarTREC data archive. Coverage is two US inland waterway systems. Access: free under CC BY 4.0. Outcome: a well-scheduled series of maintenance actions markedly raised lock availability and system throughput in the case study. Limitations: results come from simulation with ten replications, and the simulation code is not in the deposit. It is related to the USACE lock characteristics and national waterway network data catalogued here.
